-- A typed web server with process-based concurrency

type Request =
  | Get(String)
  | Post(String, Body)

type Response =
  | Ok(Body)
  | NotFound
  | Error(String)

fn handle(req: Request) -> Response = match req with
  | Get("/health")    -> Ok("ok")
  | Get(path)         -> lookup(path)
  | Post(path, body)  -> store(path, body)

fn counter(count: Int) -> Int = receive
  | Increment(n) -> counter(count + n)
  | GetCount     -> count
  | Shutdown     -> count

fn main() -> Result[Unit, Error] =
  let pid = spawn(counter, 0)
  let server = listen(8080, handle)
  supervise([pid, server], OneForOne)

Core Principles

Strict Types

Full Hindley-Milner inference with algebraic data types. No nulls, no exceptions — only typed values.

Ownership

Rust-style affine types without a borrow checker. Move semantics prevent data races at compile time.

Processes

Erlang-style lightweight processes with typed message passing. Supervision trees built into the language.

Expression-Oriented

Everything is an expression. Pattern matching, if/else, and blocks all return values.

Immutable First

Values are immutable by default. Mutation is explicit, scoped, and tracked by the type system.

Pipe-Forward

Data flows left-to-right with |> pipes. Function composition with >>. No nested parentheses.

Simple Syntax

Go-level readability with ML-level power. Minimal keywords, consistent structure, no ceremony.

Language DNA

JAPL combines the best ideas from four language families into one coherent design.

ML / Haskell

Type System

Hindley-Milner inference, algebraic data types, pattern matching, type classes as traits.

Rust

Ownership

Affine types, move semantics, zero-cost abstractions, WASM compilation target.

Erlang / Elixir

Concurrency

Lightweight processes, message passing, supervision trees, fault tolerance.

Go

Simplicity

Fast compilation, minimal syntax, easy tooling, single-binary deployment.

Compiler Architecture

A multi-stage pipeline from source to WASM, with type checking at every stage.
